description: Incident repro from Khan/frontend PR #9241 (SEC-619 Row 39, reviewed at head fd418cdb5fd4; the involved workflow file is byte-stable across every commit in the PR, so any revision reproduces it). The PR adds a new CI workflow .github/workflows/validate-workflows.yml that runs on the pull_request trigger, declares contents/pull-requests/issues: write, checks out the untrusted PR head (ref: github.event.pull_request.head.ref) with a privileged bot PAT (secrets.KHAN_ACTIONS_BOT_TOKEN), then executes code from that checked-out head (pnpm install via ./.github/actions/setup runs arbitrary lifecycle scripts, and pnpm fix-workflows runs dev/tools/fix-workflows.ts from the PR branch) and finally git push`es back to the branch -- the pwn-request combination (untrusted PR code gaining a write-scoped token and pushing). NOTE: PR #9241 is itself a pinning-hardening change -- it SHA-pins every third-party action and adds this very linter to enforce pinning -- so there is deliberately no unpinned-action spec here; the reproduced defect is the auto-fixer workflow the hardening PR introduces. The setup and run-and-commit composite actions and fix-workflows.ts are staged in the tree as the discoverability chain for what untrusted code the job actually runs.

evidence_trace: .github/workflows/validate-workflows.yml:17-21 grants the job contents: write, pull-requests: write, issues: write
.github/workflows/validate-workflows.yml:28-31 checks out the untrusted PR head (ref: github.event.pull_request.head.ref) with a privileged bot PAT (secrets.KHAN_ACTIONS_BOT_TOKEN)
.github/workflows/validate-workflows.yml:34 ./.github/actions/setup runs pnpm install, executing arbitrary lifecycle scripts from the checked-out PR
.github/workflows/validate-workflows.yml:43 pnpm fix-workflows runs dev/tools/fix-workflows.ts from the PR branch; line 53 git push`es the result back with the bot PAT
finding.failure_scenario: A contributor (or a compromised contributor token) opens a PR editing dev/tools/fix-workflows.ts, package.json scripts, or the ./.github/actions/setup action and touching any .github/**/*.yml file. The validate-workflows job checks out that untrusted PR head and runs the attacker's code -- via pnpm install lifecycle scripts and pnpm fix-workflows -- while holding secrets.KHAN_ACTIONS_BOT_TOKEN with contents: write, then git push`es. The attacker achieves arbitrary code execution with a write-scoped bot PAT, letting them push to protected branches and exfiltrate the bot's secrets -- privilege escalation beyond the PR author's own access.
finding.model_authored_prose: This workflow is a pwn-request: it runs on `pull_request`, grants `contents: write` (plus `pull-requests`/`issues: write`), checks out the untrusted PR head (`ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}`) with the privileged `KHAN_ACTIONS_BOT_TOKEN`, and then executes code from that head -- `pnpm install` (arbitrary lifecycle scripts) via `./.github/actions/setup` and `pnpm fix-workflows` (`dev/tools/fix-workflows.ts` from the PR branch) -- before `git push`ing back. Any PR that edits the fixer script, a package script, or the setup action gets arbitrary code execution holding a write-scoped bot PAT. For same-repo branch PRs the secret and write token are live, so this is exploitable by any contributor or compromised token, not just a maintainer. Do not run untrusted PR code under a write-scoped privileged token: gate the autofix behind a trusted trigger, drop `contents: write`/the bot PAT from the untrusted path, or run the linter read-only and comment rather than push.

prContext.title: 🚨 Setup GitHub Actions via unified setup action and fix-workflows linter
prContext.description:
## Summary

Creates a new composite \`setup\` action that consolidates the previously-scattered
checkout, pnpm, Node.js, GCloud auth, base-commit detection, and Cypress install
steps into a single reusable action. Removes the now-superseded \`fetch-base-commit\`
and \`shared-node-cache\` composite actions.

Also adds a \`validate-workflows\` CI workflow and \`dev/tools/fix-workflows.ts\`
linter that enforces the rule: every \`actions/checkout\` must be immediately
followed by \`./.github/actions/setup\`. Violations are auto-fixed and committed
back to the PR branch.

**This is PR 1 of 2.** DNS-based network lockdown (\`secure-network.sh\`,
allowlists, and \`allowed-domains\` input) lands separately in [PR 2](https://github.com/Khan/frontend/pull/9438) on branch
\`FEI-7556.2\`, which is based on this one.

Reviewers: #frontend-infra-web, #cypress

Issue: FEI-7556

## Test plan

These are CI/CD infrastructure changes only — no local verification path exists.

After landing, monitor the first set of workflow runs (especially \`build-and-deploy\`,
\`set-default\`, \`update-graphql-types\`, and \`static-service-e2e-base\`) to confirm
the consolidated setup action is working correctly.

## Review plan

Please review these changes:

1. 🚨 [\`.github/actions/setup/action.yml\`](https://github.com/Khan/frontend/pull/9241#discussion_r2962722608) — new unified composite action
2. 🚨 [\`.github/workflows/validate-workflows.yml\`](https://github.com/Khan/frontend/pull/9241#discussion_r2962724979) — new linter CI workflow
3. 🚨 [\`dev/tools/fix-workflows.ts\`](https://github.com/Khan/frontend/pull/9241#discussion_r2962725566) — auto-fix tool

### Common patterns

**22 Files:** All workflow jobs converted from multiple separate action calls to the
unified \`.github/actions/setup\`:

```yaml
# Before (multiple separate action calls):
- uses: actions/checkout@...
- uses: ./.github/actions/shared-node-cache
- name: Install pnpm ...
- name: Use Node.js ...

# After (single unified action):
- name: Setup
  uses: ./.github/actions/setup
  with:
      ssh-key: \${{ secrets.KHAN_ACTIONS_BOT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      setup-gcloud: "true"
```
